title: Counting the Plates

patient.name: Ms Nurul Aini binte Rahman
patient.presenting_complaint: Colour vision screening required before a clinical placement; has never been tested

history.hpc: Ms Nurul attends for colour vision screening before a healthcare placement. She says: 'Never do colour test before, I think I'm okay one.' She has no visual complaints. The OT must administer the Ishihara test correctly for each eye and document the number of plates read correctly.

investigations.colour_vision_ishihara: Ishihara plates administered in good, consistent lighting, each eye tested separately, a few seconds per plate, no coaching. Documented as the number of plates read correctly per eye. She read all test plates correctly in both eyes — a normal screen.

diagnosis: Normal colour vision screen on the Ishihara test (all plates read correctly, both eyes). The OT competency is correct, standardised administration and accurate per-eye documentation, with the doctor confirming interpretation if needed.

immediate: Explain the task: identify the number formed by the coloured dots on each plate
Ensure good, consistent lighting and that no tinted lenses are worn
Test each eye separately, present plates at the recommended distance, allow only a few seconds per plate
Avoid coaching or hinting to keep the screen valid
Document the number of plates read correctly for each eye
Report the documented result for review/certification as required
follow_up: Provide the documented result for the placement requirement
If any plates were missed, refer for fuller colour vision assessment and doctor interpretation
File the result in the record
patient_education: Explain the test checks the ability to distinguish certain colours (commonly red-green)
Reassure her the test is quick and painless
Explain the result will be documented for her placement
If abnormal, explain calmly that further testing would be arranged

key_points: Confirms the purpose of the screening (clinical placement)
Confirms no visual complaints and asks about family history of colour blindness
Confirms she has not been tested before
Explains the procedure to the patient
Ensures good lighting and that no tinted lenses are worn
Tests each eye separately with correct plate presentation and timing
Documents the number of plates read correctly per eye
Recognises all plates correct as a normal colour vision screen
Understands the Ishihara test screens for red-green deficiency
Knows a reduced plate count would require further assessment
Defers formal interpretation/certification to the doctor where needed
Provides the result for the placement requirement
Explains the test and outcome to the patient
Refers appropriately if any plates are missed
